thread:
maria: Heads-up — working on a new console view that surfaces request-level latency and routing-policy heatmaps. While wiring runtime inputs I noticed request IDs are inconsistent between edge, runtime, and telemetry. Need cross-team decision on a single correlation header + sampling rules so dashboards are reliable.

aj: What headers are we currently honoring? We have `X-Request-ID`, `traceparent` (OTel), and the runtime sometimes emits `x-rw-reqid`. We should standardize instead of adding many ad-hoc names.

kevin: SRE POV — we need 100% request-id propagation for logs/rollups. Traces can be sampled. For the console we want stable correlation_id available in metrics so rollups (errors by request, top slow paths) are accurate. Can we set it at ingress and mirror everywhere?

maria: Proposal: standard header `x-rw-correlation-id` (UUIDv4). Edge will accept `X-Request-ID`/`traceparent` and copy into `x-rw-correlation-id` if present, otherwise generate. Runtime and downstream services MUST propagate `x-rw-correlation-id`. Also: add a sticky sampling hint header `x-rw-sample: 1` when a request gets chosen to be traced. Draft sampling policy: global random sample 0.5% (or 1% if we prefer), 100% for error/exception paths and for canary routes, 10% for high-latency requests, and allow per-customer override via config.

aj: Implementation note: cheap to generate/mirror headers. We'll add support in the runtime to mirror `X-Request-ID` -> `x-rw-correlation-id` and to emit `correlation_id` in structured logs. Back-compat: if only `X-Request-ID` exists, we mirror it. Also we'll respect `traceparent` but keep correlation separate.

sasha: From product/rollouts UX — we need to filter dashboards by rollout tag (canary|stable) and by route/model variant. Does `x-rw-rollout` header exist? We currently tag requests in the router metadata. Can runtime surface that header/field into telemetry?

jasper: We can add `x-rw-rollout` propagation from the router. Note: quota checks run before routing, so if quotas need rollout info in metrics we must attach a best-effort `rollout` tag at the quota layer or emit a separate metric when routing completes. Sampling policy should be configurable per-customer and per-route.

kevin: Telemetry pipeline asks that events include `correlation_id`, `route`, `rollout_tag`, `sample_decision`, and `sample_reason`. `sample_decision` should be `0` or `1` and `sample_reason` values like `random-0.5%`, `error`, `canary`. That makes it easy to backfill in dashboards and to compute true sampled/un-sampled ratios.

maria: Dashboard fields we want: `correlation_id`, `route`, `rollout_tag`, `model_variant`, `latency_p50/p90/p99`, `tokens_out`, `error_flag`, and `sampled_trace` boolean. For un-sampled requests we still need reliable rollups by route; correlation_id is primarily for drill-down and linking span logs.

aj: One caveat: customer-supplied correlation IDs may be extremely high-cardinality. UX/infra should avoid exploding dashboards by defaulting to hashed IDs for drill-down and limiting cardinality on default views. Dashboard should default to aggregated views (by route/rollout) and allow opt-in drilldowns.

sasha: :thumbsup: agree — default aggregated. Drill-downs behind a permission or costs warning.

kevin: Action items — runtime: add header propagation and `x-rw-sample` + `x-rw-rollout` (aj, jasper); infra/telemetry: accept new fields, update parsing + schema (kevin, leena); console/product: update filters and create a canary dashboard view (maria, sasha).

maria: I'll open the GH issue with header spec + sampling configuration and attach example proto for metrics. @aj @jasper please comment on the runtime API/back-compat plan by EOD tomorrow.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: pushed branch `feature/propagate-correlation` to eng-runtime (CI: queued).

aj: Also thinking about header-loss detection — we should add `x-rw-hop` incrementing counter so we can detect if proxies strip/replace headers. Runtime can log `header_retained: true|false` for telemetry.

jasper: Good call — will add tests asserting header retention across internal proxies and a small fuzzer that drops headers to verify fallback behavior.

maria: Thanks all. Quick sync tomorrow 11:00 for a short alignment. Quick poll: prefer sampling default `1%` (react with :one:) or `0.5%` (react with :five:).
